title: GPS coordinates enable child identification
description: Live GPS coordinates transmitted from the child's device can uniquely identify the child and reveal sensitive location information including home, school, and daily routines.
assumptions: GPS data is transmitted without additional anonymization or pseudonymization

title: Unauthorized disclosure of location data
description: GPS coordinates transmitted over the network could be intercepted by unauthorized parties, leading to disclosure of the child's real-time location.
assumptions: Data transmission may not be fully encrypted or could be vulnerable to network attacks

title: Location data aggregation creates detailed movement profile
description: Regular GPS transmissions can be aggregated over time to build a comprehensive profile of the child's movements, habits, and patterns of life.
assumptions: Backend stores and processes historical location data

title: Child/guardian unaware of location tracking extent
description: The child or their guardians may not be fully aware of the frequency, duration, or purposes of GPS data collection and transmission.
assumptions: Privacy notices may not clearly explain continuous location tracking

title: Potential non-compliance with children's privacy regulations
description: Collection of children's location data may violate regulations such as COPPA, GDPR-K, or other child privacy laws requiring parental consent and data minimization.
assumptions: App may not have proper parental consent mechanisms or data retention policies

title: Location data enables cross-context linking
description: GPS coordinates can be linked with other data sources to create a more complete profile of the child across different contexts and services.
assumptions: Location data may be combined with other identifiers or datasets

title: Location pings can be linked to identify individual users
description: Location history data written to the store can be linked across time and sessions to create comprehensive movement profiles of individual users, enabling tracking of daily routines, habits, and associations.
assumptions: Location data includes sufficient granularity (coordinates, timestamps) to enable user identification through pattern analysis

title: Location data can directly identify individuals
description: Location history is highly identifying personal data that can reveal home addresses, workplaces, medical visits, and other sensitive information about specific individuals.
assumptions: Location pings are associated with user accounts or device identifiers

title: Unauthorized access to location history store
description: If the Location History Store lacks proper access controls, unauthorized parties could access stored location data, leading to privacy breaches.
assumptions: Data store may have insufficient authentication/authorization mechanisms

title: Implicit disclosure through location metadata
description: Storing location pings creates implicit disclosure of personal data through metadata (timestamps, frequency, patterns) that can reveal sensitive information beyond explicit location coordinates.
assumptions: Location data includes metadata that can be analyzed to infer additional personal information

title: Users unaware of continuous location logging
description: Users may not be fully aware that their location is being continuously logged and stored in the Location History Store, or the extent of data collection.
assumptions: Privacy notices may not clearly communicate the scope and purpose of location data collection

title: Lack of user control over stored location data
description: Users may have limited ability to view, delete, or control how their location history is stored and used once written to the Location History Store.
assumptions: System may not provide adequate user controls for data management

title: Excessive location data collection for geofencing
description: The Geofencing Engine receives continuous location pings from the Mobile App Backend. This may violate data minimization principles if the engine collects more location data than strictly necessary for zone entry/exit detection (e.g., collecting precise coordinates when zone-level granularity would suffice, or retaining historical location data beyond what's needed for the geofencing function).
assumptions: Geofencing Engine stores or processes location data beyond immediate zone-checking requirements

title: User identification through location patterns
description: Location pings forwarded to the Geofencing Engine could enable identification of individual users through their movement patterns, even if explicit identifiers are not included. Location data is inherently identifying when combined with temporal patterns and known user behaviors.
assumptions: Location data contains sufficient granularity to enable user identification through pattern analysis

title: User unawareness of location data forwarding
description: Users may not be aware that their location pings are being forwarded from the Mobile App Backend to a separate Geofencing Engine process. This lack of transparency about internal data flows could violate user expectations and informed consent principles.
assumptions: Privacy policy or user interface does not clearly disclose internal data flow to geofencing component

title: Potential GDPR/regulatory non-compliance for location processing
description: Processing location data for geofencing may require specific legal basis under GDPR (e.g., explicit consent for special category data processing). The flow from Backend to Geofencing Engine may not have proper documentation of lawful basis, data retention policies, or user rights mechanisms.
assumptions: Location data processing lacks proper GDPR compliance documentation and user consent mechanisms
uncertainty_note: Depends on jurisdiction and specific implementation details not provided in flow description

title: Unauthorized disclosure of family location zone data
description: The Family Account Store contains sensitive location zone definitions (home, school, friend's house) that could be disclosed to unauthorized parties if the data flow to the Geofencing Engine is intercepted or if the store is compromised. This reveals precise locations where family members spend time.
assumptions: Data flow is not encrypted or access controls are insufficient

title: Identifiability of family members through zone data
description: Zone definitions combined with permission data in the Family Account Store could identify specific family members and their routines. An attacker could determine which zones belong to which individuals based on access patterns and zone configurations.
assumptions: Zone data is linked to individual family member accounts

title: Aggregation of location data for profiling
description: Multiple zone definitions (home, school, friend's house) stored in DS2 can be aggregated to build comprehensive profiles of family members' daily routines, movement patterns, and social connections, enabling detailed behavioral profiling.
assumptions: Multiple zone types are stored and accessible

title: Unawareness of location data access by family members
description: Family members may be unaware that their location zone preferences are being read by the Geofencing Engine, especially if consent mechanisms are unclear or if data access occurs without explicit notification.
assumptions: Privacy notices do not clearly explain data flows to geofencing services

title: Location data linkable to child identity
description: Geofencing notifications sent to the parent link the child's location movements (zone entry/exit events) to their identity, creating a persistent link between location data and personal identity.
assumptions: Notifications contain or can be correlated with child identification information

title: Unauthorized disclosure of location notifications
description: Location-based arrival/departure notifications could be intercepted during transmission from the Geofencing Engine to the parent, exposing the child's location data to unauthorized parties.
assumptions: Transmission channel may not be fully secured

title: Location data aggregation over time
description: Multiple geofencing notifications over time can be aggregated to build a detailed profile of the child's movement patterns, daily routines, and behavioral habits.
assumptions: Notifications are stored or logged by the parent or system

title: Child unaware of location monitoring
description: The child may not be aware that their location is being continuously monitored and that notifications are being sent to the parent when they enter or exit defined zones.
assumptions: Child is a minor and may not have been informed about the tracking system

title: Excessive Data Collection for Storage
description: The backend stores account, child profile, and geofence zone data in DS2. This may violate the minimality principle if data collected exceeds what is strictly necessary for the application's functionality. Child profile and geofence data are sensitive personal data that should be minimized.
assumptions: Assuming the application collects and stores all available child profile and geofence data without strict necessity review

title: Identifiable Child Profile Data Storage
description: Child profile data stored in DS2 may contain personally identifiable information (PII) that could be used to identify specific children. This creates identifiability risks if the datastore is compromised or accessed without authorization.
assumptions: Child profile data includes PII such as names, ages, or other identifying characteristics

title: User Unawareness of Data Storage
description: Users may not be fully aware of what account, child profile, and geofence zone data is being stored in DS2, or how long it is retained. This lack of transparency prevents informed consent.
assumptions: Privacy notices may not clearly explain all data types being stored or retention periods

title: Limited User Control Over Stored Data
description: Users may have limited ability to access, modify, or delete their account, child profile, and geofence data stored in DS2. This reduces user autonomy over their personal information.
assumptions: The application may not provide comprehensive data management controls for all stored data types

title: Unauthorized disclosure of child's location data
description: The Mobile App Backend may disclose the child's current location or location history to the parent without proper authorization checks, or the data may be intercepted during transmission. Location data is highly sensitive personal information that could reveal the child's whereabouts, routines, and habits.
assumptions: Parent has legitimate access rights to view child's location; transmission is over network

title: Location data aggregation reveals child's patterns
description: Location history data requested by the parent can be aggregated over time to reveal detailed patterns about the child's movements, daily routines, social connections, and behavioral habits, creating a comprehensive profile beyond what was intended to be shared.
assumptions: Location history is stored and can be retrieved in bulk

title: Child unaware of location tracking and sharing
description: The child may be unaware that their location is being tracked by the app and shared with the parent. This lack of awareness prevents the child from understanding what data is collected, how it's used, or exercising any control over their location privacy.
assumptions: Child is a minor and may not have been informed about location tracking

title: Potential non-compliance with child privacy regulations
description: Location tracking and sharing of a child's data may violate privacy regulations such as COPPA (Children's Online Privacy Protection Act) or GDPR-K (children's provisions), which require parental consent, data minimization, and specific protections for minors' location data.
assumptions: Child is under applicable age threshold for child privacy laws
uncertainty_note: Depends on jurisdiction and specific implementation of consent mechanisms

title: Child's identity revealed through location data
description: The child's location data, when accessed by the parent, inherently reveals the child's identity and can be used to identify them in various contexts. Location patterns can also be used to infer the child's identity even if not explicitly named.
assumptions: Location data is associated with child's account/profile

title: Unauthorized disclosure of location history during retrieval
description: Location history data retrieved from the data store could be intercepted or exposed during transmission to the backend, or accessed by unauthorized personnel within the backend system. Location data is highly sensitive personal information.
assumptions: Data is transmitted over network; backend has access controls

title: Location history used beyond intended purpose
description: The backend may use retrieved location history for purposes beyond serving the parent's map/history view, such as profiling, analytics, or sharing with third parties without explicit consent.
assumptions: Backend has discretion over data usage; no strict purpose limitation enforced

title: Parents unaware of location data retrieval and processing
description: Parents may not be fully informed about when, how, and why their child's location history is being retrieved from storage, limiting their ability to make informed privacy decisions.
assumptions: Privacy notices may not detail specific data retrieval operations

title: Location history linked to other personal data
description: Retrieved location history could be linked with other personal data about the child or family, creating comprehensive profiles that reveal sensitive patterns about daily life, routines, and associations.
assumptions: Backend has access to multiple data sources; data correlation is possible

title: Linkability between parent, secondary guardian, and child
description: The invitation flow creates linkability between the parent (EE1), the secondary guardian being invited, and the child's location data. This enables correlation of identities and activities across multiple parties.
assumptions: The backend processes and stores the invitation relationship

title: Direct identification of parent and secondary guardian
description: The parent's identity and the secondary guardian's identity are transmitted to the backend, making both parties directly identifiable in the system.
assumptions: Identity information is included in the invitation request

title: Disclosure of child location sharing intent
description: The backend receives and processes information about which parties are authorized to view the child's location, disclosing sensitive access control information.
assumptions: The backend stores invitation records and access permissions

title: Unawareness of data processing by secondary guardian
description: The secondary guardian may not be fully aware of what data will be processed about them or the child when accepting the invitation, including location tracking scope and duration.
assumptions: Consent and transparency mechanisms may be insufficient

title: Potential non-compliance with child privacy regulations
description: Sharing child location data with additional guardians may require specific consent mechanisms under regulations like COPPA or GDPR-K, which may not be properly implemented.
assumptions: Regulatory requirements for child location data sharing apply
uncertainty_note: Regulatory applicability depends on jurisdiction and specific implementation

title: Location data linkability to child identity
description: The child's live location data shared with the secondary guardian can be linked to the child's identity, creating a persistent link between location history and personal identity that could be used to track movements over time.
assumptions: Location data contains sufficient precision to identify the child's whereabouts

title: Unauthorized disclosure of child's location
description: The child's live location could be disclosed to unauthorized parties if the secondary guardian shares it further, or if there's a security breach in the backend system during transmission.
assumptions: Secondary guardian may not have adequate security controls; transmission could be intercepted

title: Location data aggregation creating movement profile
description: Multiple location data points shared over time can be aggregated to create a detailed movement profile of the child, revealing patterns about their daily routine, habits, and frequented locations.
assumptions: Location data is shared continuously or frequently over time

title: Child unaware of location sharing with secondary guardian
description: The child may not be aware that their live location is being shared with a secondary guardian, or may not understand the scope and implications of this data sharing.
assumptions: Child may not have been informed or may not comprehend the data sharing

title: Non-repudiation of location data sharing
description: There may be insufficient audit trails to prove whether location data was shared with the secondary guardian, or when and what specific data was transmitted.
assumptions: System may not maintain comprehensive logs of data sharing events

title: Linkability of analytics data to user profiles
description: Aggregated usage and engagement analytics shared with advertising partners can be linked to other data sources to build comprehensive user profiles, enabling cross-service tracking and behavioral profiling.
assumptions: Advertising partners maintain user profiles and can correlate analytics data with other identifiers

title: Re-identification from aggregated analytics
description: Even aggregated analytics data can potentially be de-anonymized through re-identification attacks, especially when combined with other data sources held by advertising partners.
assumptions: Sufficient auxiliary data exists for re-identification attacks on aggregated datasets

title: Data aggregation across multiple sources
description: Analytics data from this flow contributes to advertising partners' ability to aggregate data from multiple apps and services, creating detailed user profiles beyond what users expect.
assumptions: Advertising partners aggregate data from multiple third-party sources

title: User unawareness of data sharing extent
description: Users may not fully understand that 'aggregated analytics' are shared with advertising partners, or the extent to which this data can be used for profiling and targeted advertising.
assumptions: Privacy policies do not clearly communicate the implications of analytics data sharing

title: Potential regulatory non-compliance
description: Sharing usage analytics with advertising partners may violate privacy regulations (GDPR, CCPA) if proper consent mechanisms, data minimization, or purpose limitation are not implemented.
assumptions: Regulatory requirements for third-party data sharing are not fully met
uncertainty_note: Depends on specific consent and compliance measures in place

title: Location data linkability across check-in events
description: Multiple check-in/SOS messages with location data from the child can be linked together to create a movement profile or track the child's patterns over time, potentially revealing sensitive information about their routines, locations visited, and behavioral patterns.
assumptions: Child sends multiple check-in messages over time; backend stores historical location data

title: Child identifiability from location and check-in data
description: The child's identity can be directly identified from the check-in/SOS messages combined with their location data, especially when linked to their account in the backend system.
assumptions: Child account is linked to their identity in the system

title: Attributable check-in/SOS messages
description: Check-in and SOS messages can be attributed to the specific child who sent them, creating non-repudiation evidence that could be used to hold the child accountable for their actions or location at specific times.
assumptions: System maintains audit logs or message attribution records

title: Unauthorized disclosure of child location data
description: If the Mobile App Backend is compromised or has inadequate access controls, the child's location data from check-in/SOS messages could be disclosed to unauthorized parties, creating safety risks for the child.
assumptions: Backend stores location data; potential for security vulnerabilities

title: Tampering with location data in transit or storage
description: Location data in check-in/SOS messages could be modified during transmission or while stored in the backend, potentially leading to incorrect location information being shown to parents, which could have serious safety implications.
assumptions: Data transmitted over network; stored in backend database

title: Non-compliance with child privacy regulations
description: Collecting and processing location data from children may violate privacy regulations such as COPPA (US) or GDPR-K (EU) if proper consent mechanisms, data minimization, and parental controls are not implemented.
assumptions: System operates in jurisdictions with child privacy laws; location data is considered sensitive
